title: an object cache's freelist array was sized by the cached object's size instead of a pointer's
object: the object cache's freelist array of void*, one direct calloc
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: an array of pointers sized by the element the pointers point AT
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc/calloc/realloc, with neither slabs.c nor cache.c between it and the request.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: `grep -c 'calloc(initial_pool_size' ` on 1.6.45:cache.c is 0. The construct was REMOVED rather than fixed -- 1.6.45's cache_create allocates no pool array at all, the freelist being a STAILQ threaded through the free objects themselves -- so the pinned code cannot carry the defect. A fix-reversal against history.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at the labelled probe on the buggy arm and is silent on the fixed arm -- keyed on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string AddressSanitizer.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x1023a8, with supervise resolving `expect mch_write_probe 0x102390` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions. Capstone measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-capstone/): spatial CAUGHT, sublet CAUGHT.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- this is not a slab chunk and not a cache.c object -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the crossed object is the object cache's own BOOKKEEPING, not an object from it -- which is why this row is plain and not nested. The slot count promised by `freetotal` is correct; it is the per-slot WIDTH that is wrong, so the shortfall scales with how small the cached object is.
